brief: HF flows: DM equity buying was funded by Asia selling. US equities saw the largest net buying in 5 weeks, led by Tech, having earlier been flagged as light versus Asia; Mag-7 inflows over the past month pushed net allocations back near peak levels, and Software was the most net-bought sub-sector. European equities were net bought at the fastest pace in 5 months, driven by short covers and concentrated in Industrials, Tech and Discretionary, though net allocations remain near 5-year trough levels. Citing Peter Oppenheimer, GS keeps a constructive medium-term equity view despite rising yields and compressed equity risk premia, since compute demand outstrips supply, lowering earnings-bubble risk; GS's base case has SPX EPS growing 11% in both 2027 (to $415) and 2028 ($460). Separately: Chinese exports enter overseas markets at an average 30% discount, then prices rose in 7 of 11 sectors post-entry; GS projects aggregate ex-China market share rising from 18% to 31% by 2035, upside it calls largely unpriced, especially in "Latecomer" categories. A separate note flags 42 India-listed names leveraged to domestic AI infrastructure, up 60% YTD versus NIFTY -11%, accounting for about 40% of NIFTY 500's capex growth this year.
